**Hydrogen – Key Properties**

| Property | Value / Description |
|----------|---------------------|
| **Atomic number** | 1 |
| **Symbol** | H |
| **Atomic mass** | 1.00794 u (average) |
| **Molar mass** | 1.008 g mol⁻¹ |
| **Electron configuration** | 1s¹ |
| **Electronegativity (Pauling)** | 2.20 |
| **First ionization energy** | 13.598 eV (1312 kJ mol⁻¹) |
| **Second ionization energy** | 27.211 eV (2625 kJ mol⁻¹) |
| **Electron affinity** | –72.8 kJ mol⁻¹ (negative, meaning energy is released when H⁻ is formed) |
| **Boiling point** | –252.87 °C (120.95 K) |
| **Melting point** | –259.16 °C (14.01 K) |
| **Density at STP** | 0.08988 g L⁻¹ (0.00008988 g cm⁻³) |
| **Specific heat capacity (gas, 298 K)** | 28.836 J mol⁻¹ K⁻¹ |
| **Heat of formation (gas)** | 0 kJ mol⁻¹ (by definition) |
| **Bond dissociation energy (H₂)** | 436 kJ mol⁻¹ |
| **Dipole moment (H₂)** | 0 (non‑polar) |
| **Isotopes** | H‑1 (protium), H‑2 (deuterium, D), H‑3 (tritium, T) |
| **Common oxidation states** | +1 (as H⁺ or in hydrides), –1 (as H⁻ in metal hydrides) |
| **Physical state at room temperature** | Gas |
| **Reactivity** | Highly reactive; forms covalent bonds with nonmetals, ionic bonds with metals, and participates in acid–base chemistry as H⁺ (proton). |
| **Spectral lines** | Lyman series (UV), Balmer series (visible), Paschen series (IR) – key in astrophysics. |
| **Role in biology** | Essential component of water (H₂O), organic molecules, and metabolic processes. |
| **Energy carrier** | Used in fuel cells (electrochemical conversion of H₂ to electricity). |
